newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sierra Leone seeks expanded ties with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone seeks expanded ties with Iran.

text.p: Sierra Leone President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah said on Monday during a visit to Iran that his country wanted to expand ties with the Islamic republic in all areas, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
It said Kabbah, who started his four-day visit to Iran on Sunday, made the remarks after meeting Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
"Expressing his satisfaction over...the two countries' relations, Kabbah told reporters Sierra Leone is determined to upgrade bilateral cooperation in all areas", it said.
Rafsanjani said Iran was keen on ties with African countries and in particular Sierra Leone, which "is rich in natural resources, most of which have remained untapped.."
He said Iran was ready to help Sierra Leone in sectors including mines, industries, agriculture and education.
In June, Iran agreed to help develop Sierra Leone's fishing industry and provided eight fishing boats along with experts.
Kabbah has built up ties with Iran since taking office in March. Officials say Tehran is paying for Kabbah's visit.

Mineral Resources Minister Alex Harding told state radio recently that Iranian investors were inspecting government diamond mines in the east and a southern bauxite mine, put out of action in 1995 by rebels.
